title: yadgar/iam
$comment: Closure is PER CHART (ADR-0850): this file closes the key set this chart owns and nothing upstream or downstream of it. `additionalProperties: false` sits at the root and at every declared block, so a misspelled key anywhere in the tree is refused by name instead of silently dropped or silently accepted. OPEN (no `properties`, no closure): `global`, because helm injects it into every subchart and the parent owns its closure; this chart reads only `global.hostname`, through `templates/_hostname.tpl` (`.context.Values.global`, ADR-0808); `resources` and `rollingUpdate`, because the shape they take is the Kubernetes API's and this chart only forwards it through `toYaml`/`with`. EXTRAS (leaves `chart/values.yaml` never states, read straight off the templates): `image.digest`, rewritten at package time by ci-release (D65), read in `templates/deployment.yaml`; `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace`, read in `templates/networkpolicy.yaml`, with `values.yaml` shipping the parent block `scrapeFrom: {}` empty; `tls.clientCaSecret` and `tls.clientCaSecretKey` (B-U5E expand, kept by B-U5: `templates/deployment.yaml` renders the CA env, mount and volume only when `tls.enabled` is true and `clientCaSecret` names a Secret). Types, toggle shapes and `required` are NOT this file's job (ADR-0847): `render-checks.yaml` owns them, and `autoscaling`/`autoscaling.enabled`'s `kindIs` guards (ledger 1135) are the worked example — a schema `type` on either would refuse the chart's own default render the day the value changed shape, which is why every leaf here is `{}`. Four exceptions, plus `tls.clientAuth`'s `required`. `credential.lifetimeSeconds` (ADR-0972 (3)) is an untyped `{}` leaf in a closed block: its whole-number, positive and ten-year-bound refusals are named sentences in `templates/render-checks.yaml`, which a schema `type` or `minimum` would pre-empt. `tls.enabled`, `iamDb.tls.enabled` (ADR-0845, C-SVb) and, from B-N3 (ADR-0852, ADR-0885), `nats.tls.enabled` keep `type: boolean` and their parent blocks keep `required: [enabled]`: `required` alone passes a null value through, so the leaf needs its type too (K-1) — `templates/render-checks.yaml` still carries the `hasKey`/`kindIs` guard that produces ADR-0845's own named sentence, because a schema refusal and a render-check refusal report differently and both are asserted. `nats.tls`'s other keys (`caSecret`, `caSecretKey`, `clientCertSecret`, `clientCertSecretKey`, `clientKeySecretKey`) are untyped `{}` leaves with real defaults in `values.yaml`, the same shape `iamDb.tls`'s equivalents take — ADR-0885 gives the broker hop its OWN client-identity key, independent of `iamDb.tls.clientCertSecret`, because this chart's only client-leaf mount before B-N3 was `iamDb`'s own and coupling the two would make turning either hop's TLS off also turn the other's identity off, silently. `nats.tls` carries no `domain` key, unlike `iamDb.tls`: `async-nats` verifies the broker's certificate against the host in `nats.url` and has no override, so a `nats.tls.domain` key would configure a variable the binary refuses outright (`NATS_TLS_DOMAIN`). `tls.clientAuth` (B-U5, ADR-0854 extending ADR-0845) is listed in `tls.required` and stays an untyped `{}` leaf (coordinator ruling R1, ADR-0847): the binary refuses an absent `LISTEN_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH`, so the chart has no default and the schema refuses the absent key; a `type` or `enum` here would pre-empt the named sentences in `templates/render-checks.yaml` for a bare `off` (YAML reads it as false), any other non-string and an unknown mode, so those shapes are refused there by name, beside the cross-key refusal a schema cannot state (a verifying mode with no `tls.clientCaSecret`). From K1 (ADR-0972, ADR-0975) `off` is also refused while `tls.enabled` is true, and with `tls.enabled` false the chart ignores and does not validate the value and renders the constant `off`; the key stays in `tls.required`, so deleting it is a schema refusal either way. `server.limits` (ADR-1006) is typed on purpose, like `iamDb.requestTimeoutSeconds`: four required integers whose `minimum` and `maximum` are `yadgar_lifecycle::serve_tls::ServerLimits`'s own ranges, held there by `tests/chart_server_limits.rs`. The one rule a schema cannot state, `keepaliveTimeoutSeconds` below `keepaliveIntervalSeconds`, is a named sentence in `templates/render-checks.yaml`.
